title: Negative Index Laws

findings.finding: p4-q1-b and p5-q4-b repeat the same complete conversion task, a^{-4}, without an explicit retrieval or comparison purpose.
findings.breakdown: The later copy changes neither the expression nor the required decision. Its replacement must preserve the deliberate progression from a^{-4} to 2a^{-4} to (2a)^{-4}.
findings.checked: Compared both complete instructions and expressions, the earlier p3-positive-indices-part-c, and the neighbouring practice. The initial teaching occurrence supplies preparation, but no explicit purpose is stated for repeating the independent exercise task.
findings.assumptions: Variables with negative indices are nonzero. Calculator availability does not affect this finding.

repair.proposal: Change p5-q4-b, c and d together to a^{-6}, 2a^{-6} and (2a)^{-6}. Answers: 1/a^6, 2/a^6 and 1/(64a^6), respectively. This replaces the later duplicate while preserving the coefficient-and-brackets comparison.

findings.doneWhen: The later duplicate has different values and parts b–d retain their deliberate comparison.

findings.finding: Extend the coefficient-and-brackets comparison by evaluating the neighbouring expressions at the same value of a.
findings.breakdown: Numerical substitution makes the effect of including the coefficient in the powered base visible.
findings.checked: For the proposed revised exponent −6, at a=2 the values are 2/2^6=1/32 and 1/4^6=1/4096; their ratio is 128. Substitution and the required index operations use prior knowledge and this topic's practice.
findings.assumptions: This wording incorporates the duplicate repair to p5-q4-b–d.

repair.proposal: Immediately after p5-q4-d, add optional follow-up parts: (i) Find 2a^{-6} when a=2. Answer: 1/32. (ii) Find (2a)^{-6} when a=2. Answer: 1/4096. (iii) How many times as large is the first value as the second? Answer: 128.

findings.doneWhen: Each numerical comparison is a separate follow-up part using the revised question's expressions.

findings.finding: p8-q2-v repeats the complete conversion task 7/(x^{-4}y^3) from p7-practice-e without an explicit retrieval or comparison purpose.
findings.breakdown: Both prompts require the same conversion of the same expression; no values, givens or decisions change.
findings.checked: Compared the complete expressions, surrounding instructions and teaching roles. The move from the identify block to the exercise does not state a specific retrieval or comparison purpose for this unchanged task.
findings.assumptions: Both tasks are used in booklet order, with x and y nonzero.
findings.doneWhen: The later task retains the same structure with different numbers and the corresponding answer.

findings.finding: The reciprocal topic lacks a review of applying a positive outer power to both numerator and denominator, although its second worked example uses that prior law directly.
findings.breakdown: The transition from (y/x)^3 to y^3/x^3 requires recall of the quotient-power law. The new reciprocal identity incorporates that law without separately rehearsing it.
findings.checked: Searched all supplied preceding teaching and practice. Earlier practice includes powers of products, but the immediately preceding denominator topic does not rehearse powers of quotients. The positive quotient-power step is substantial and is used directly in p9-example-right-item.
findings.assumptions: Positive index laws are prior knowledge from the course's Index Laws content. Calculator availability is immaterial.

repair.proposal: Before p9-law-block, add: 'Simplify: (a) (x/y)^2; (b) (a/b)^3; (c) (m/n)^4.' Answers: x^2/y^2, a^3/b^3 and m^4/n^4. Keep the review within one page.

findings.doneWhen: Students rehearse distributing a positive power across a quotient before the reciprocal examples.

findings.finding: Add a fixed-base sequence that isolates the effect of changing the magnitude of a negative exponent.
findings.breakdown: Existing practice changes bases alongside exponents; the proposed run exposes successive powers of the reciprocal.
findings.checked: All five answers are correct. The numerical bases are nonzero, and p9 teaches the complete method. Repeating p10-q1-i within this run has an explicit comparison purpose.
findings.assumptions: The added run remains optional practice under the existing instruction.

repair.proposal: Append to p10-q1 the single instruction 'Predict how each answer will change before simplifying.' Add (u) (2/3)^{-1}, answer 3/2; (v) (2/3)^{-2}, answer 9/4; (w) (2/3)^{-3}, answer 27/8; (x) (2/3)^{-4}, answer 81/16; then the unpatterned item (y) (3/5)^{-2}, answer 25/9. The run holds the base fixed and varies only the exponent.

findings.doneWhen: The four fixed-base parts and one unpatterned follow-up appear under the existing question instruction, with only the prediction line added.

findings.finding: The closing group p11-q2-p–r moves sharply from routine single expressions to combining two powered products before the booklet's existing intermediate practice.
findings.breakdown: At p11-q2-p, students must distribute two outer powers across coefficients and two variables, handle a negative outer power, and combine the results. Earlier questions practise these components separately; p12-q4 provides intermediate combinations only afterwards.
findings.checked: Compared the full preceding teaching, p9 guided practice, p10-q1, p11-q2-a–o and p12-q4. The component methods are available, so this is a coordination jump rather than missing teaching. Being the closing group does not supply the intermediate demand that p12-q4 already offers.
findings.assumptions: Ordinary index laws and signed arithmetic are prior knowledge. The issue does not depend on calculator availability.

repair.proposal: Move p11-q2-p, p11-q2-q and p11-q2-r together to immediately after p12-q4-r. Preserve their order and the shared-expression comparison between p and r.

findings.doneWhen: The existing intermediate powered-expression practice precedes the three combined applications.

findings.finding: Extend the given-power task to reciprocal powers without requiring students to find x.
findings.breakdown: The follow-up connects x^4=3 directly to the booklet's negative-index relationship.
findings.checked: Since x^4=3, x is nonzero, x^{-4}=1/3, x^{-8}=1/9 and x^8x^{-8}=1. These values hold for either real solution of x^4=3 and require only methods available by this topic.
findings.assumptions: Use the existing given x^4=3 throughout.

repair.proposal: After p13-q10-d, add (e) Find x^{-4}. Answer: 1/3. (f) Find x^{-8}. Answer: 1/9. (g) Find x^8 × x^{-8}. Answer: 1.

findings.doneWhen: The three separate follow-up parts retain the original given and have the stated answers.

protectedGroups.observation: The coefficient stays in its original position; only the negative-index factor changes position.
protectedGroups.varies: The presence and position of the coefficient 3.
protectedGroups.invariant: The negative-index factor x⁻² and its rewrite as x² in the numerator.

protectedGroups.observation: Reciprocal starting bases raised to the same negative power produce reciprocal results.
protectedGroups.varies: The numerator and denominator exchange places.
protectedGroups.invariant: The numbers two and three and the exponent negative two.

protectedGroups.observation: The location of the negative power determines the direction of conversion; a separate coefficient retains its role.
protectedGroups.varies: Numerator versus denominator placement, then presence of coefficient 2.

protectedGroups.observation: Changing the denominator exponent changes the negative index without changing the coefficient or sign.
The denominator exponent becomes the magnitude of the negative index.
The numerical denominator, leading sign and numerator coefficient remain separate from conversion of the variable power.
protectedGroups.varies: Exponent, then sign, then numerator coefficient.

protectedGroups.observation: Brackets determine whether the coefficient belongs to the powered base.
protectedGroups.varies: Whether 2 is inside the base raised to -2.

protectedGroups.observation: Repeats the coefficient-scope contrast with another coefficient and exponent.
protectedGroups.varies: Whether 3 is inside the powered base.

protectedGroups.observation: Distinguishes the effect of the second exponent's sign from the effect of changing the operation.
protectedGroups.varies: First the sign of the second exponent, then division versus multiplication.

protectedGroups.observation: Separates an external minus from a negative base and exposes the role of odd and even powers.
protectedGroups.varies: Exponent parity and placement of the minus, one feature at each step.

protectedGroups.observation: Contrasts a retained coefficient with a coefficient raised to the negative power.
Distinguishes multiplying by 3 from dividing by 3 during reciprocal conversion.
